name: Curve-hugging nasal spray
subtitle: a nose spray that reaches the smell nerves

effects.effect: a jet clings to a curved surface beside it and follows its curve
small molecules seep through a membrane

effect: a jet clings to a curved surface beside it and follows its curve
how: Drugs sprayed high in the nose can slip into the brain along the smell nerves, skipping the barrier that blocks most brain medicines, but ordinary sprays land low and get swallowed. This nozzle fires a thin jet along the curved roof of the nostril; the jet clings to the curve and follows it up to the narrow strip where the smell nerves are, and the drug seeps through the lining there.
obstacle: Every nose is shaped differently, so the nozzle may need fitting to each patient for the jet to stay on the curve.
why: Wall-hugging jets are reliable physics; steering one inside real noses is untested.
real: Olfactory-targeted nasal devices exist (Nemera Guided Stream, circumferential-velocity spray patent) and simulations show liquid-film translocation along the wall to the olfactory region, but no Coanda-jet nozzle found.
